explain: The line is the average speed at peak hours in each year; the shaded band is the range LTA aims for. The two buttons switch between expressways and arterial roads.

Tap a point, drag across the chart, or use the slider and the arrow buttons. The card under the chart reads that year: the speed, the change from the year before, where it ranks, and how far it sits from the band.
A ringed dot marks a year outside the band. 2020 and 2021 are drawn faint: the piece did not score the pandemic years.

The sentences in the card are worked out when the page is built, from the same data file as the line. None is typed by hand and none comes from a live model, so the card and the chart cannot disagree.
panel: Each dial shows the speed in the selected year on one kind of road. The thick part of the arc is LTA's target band, and the words under the number say whether the speed is inside it.
Tap a dial to draw that road's line under it. Drag the slider, or press Play, to move through the years.
Scroll on: each step of the story under the panel moves it to that step's year.
A ringed dot marks a year outside the band. 2020 and 2021 are drawn faint: the piece did not score the pandemic years.

steps.text: 2004: expressways 62.7 km/h, arterial roads 24.8 km/h. The shaded bands are LTA's targets.
2016: arterial roads at 30.4 km/h, above the band. It happened again in 2023. The sealed bet that every scored year would sit inside the bands failed on these years.
2021: arterial roads at 32 km/h, the highest in the record. The piece did not score 2020 and 2021, the pandemic years.
2025: expressways at 55 km/h, the lowest in the record and still inside the band.
